bottom_line: At a median follow-up of 56 months, the primary outcome occurred in 1412 patients in the ramipril group (16.5%), as compared with 1423 patients in the telmisartan group (16.7%; relative risk, 1.01; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.94 to 1.09).
implications: Based on the reported primary outcome rates (16.7% vs. 16.5%) and relative risk (1.01; 95% CI, 0.94 to 1.09), the trial supports that telmisartan produced a similar primary composite outcome rate to ramipril within the study’s noninferiority framework; the CI does not support superiority of telmisartan over ramipril. Combination therapy showed no improvement in the primary outcome (relative risk, 0.99; 95% CI, 0.92 to 1.07) while showing higher adverse-event rates such as hypotensive symptoms (4.8% vs. 1.7%), syncope (0.3% vs. 0.2%), and renal dysfunction (13.5% vs. 10.2%).

major_points.text: Patients underwent double-blind randomization to ramipril, telmisartan, or combination therapy after a single-blind run-in period.
major_points.quote: After a 3-week, single-blind run-in period, patients underwent double-blind random- ization, with 8576 assigned to receive 10 mg of ramipril per day, 8542 assigned to receive 80 mg of telmisartan per day, and 8502 assigned to receive both drugs

major_points.text: The primary composite outcome was cardiovascular death, MI, stroke, or hospitalization for heart failure.
major_points.quote: The primary composite outcome was death from cardiovascular causes, myocardial infarction, stroke, or hospitalization for heart failure.

major_points.text: Telmisartan met noninferiority versus ramipril for the primary outcome based on the prespecified margin.
major_points.quote: The upper boundary of the confidence interval (1.09) for the relative risk of the primary outcome in the telmisartan group as compared with the ramipril group was sig- nificantly lower than the predefined noninferior- ity boundary of 1.13 (P = 0.004).

major_points.text: Combination therapy did not improve the primary outcome versus ramipril but increased key adverse events including hypotensive symptoms, syncope, and renal dysfunction.
major_points.quote: In the combination-therapy group, the primary outcome occurred in 1386 patients (16.3%; relative risk, 0.99; 95% CI, 0.92 to 1.07); as compared with the ramipril group, there was an increased risk of hypotensive symptoms

major_points.text: Compared with ramipril, telmisartan was associated with lower rates of cough and angioedema but higher hypotensive symptoms; syncope rates were the same.
major_points.quote: As compared with the ramipril group, the telmisartan group had lower rates of cough (1.1% vs. 4.2%, P<0.001) and angio- edema (0.1% vs. 0.3%, P = 0.01) and a higher rate of hypotensive symptoms (2.6% vs. 1.7%, P<0.001)

criticisms.text: The trial used an active run-in phase that selected patients who tolerated both medications; discontinuation rates may be higher in clinical practice.
criticisms.quote: cause we used an active run-in phase that selected patients for randomization only if they tolerated both medications. After randomization, we vig- orously reinforced adherence and encouraged pa- tients who stopped medications to restart them. In clinical practice, the rates of discontinuation might be higher.
